Direct synthesis of indazole derivatives via
Rh(III)-catalyzed C–H activation of phthalazinones
and allenes†
Chuanliu Yin, Tianshuo Zhong, Xiangyun Zheng,
 Lianghao Li, Jian Zhou and
Chuanming Yu
 *
A novel Rh( III)-catalyzed annulation of phthalazinones or pyridazinones with various allenes was devel-
oped, leading to the formation of indazole derivatives bearing a quaternary carbon in moderate to good
yields. The targeted products were synthesized via sequential C –H activation and ole ﬁn insertion, fol-
lowed by β-hydride elimination and intramolecular cyclization. The synthetic protocol proceeded e ﬃcien-
tly with broad functional group tolerance, high atom e ﬃciency and high Z-selectivity. The practicability of
this method was proved by synthetic transformation.
Introduction
Nitrogen-containing heterocycles represent one of the most
prominent heterocyclic sca ﬀolds with their widespread distri-
bution in natural products and their close connection with
drugs.
1 Among them, indazoles and their derivatives have pri-
vileged structures for potential biological activity. 2 As shown in
Fig. 1, nigellidine has the capacity to regulate glucose con-
sumption,
3 a PDE 4/TNFR inhibitor shows anti-HAT activity, 4 a
human immunodeficiency virus protease (HIVPR) inhibitor
displays antiviral activity, 5 a tyrosine threonine kinase (TTK)
inhibitor possesses good anti-cancer activity, 6 and several
indazolones are reported to show anti-inflammatory activities. 7
Therefore, it is of great significance to develop a simple and
eﬃcient method to synthesize indazole sca ﬀolds.
Over the past decades, transition-metal-catalyzed C –H bond
activation has been considered as an increasingly significant
tool in organic synthesis, which can construct complicated
molecules through synchronous C –C and C –N bond for-
mation.
8 In particular, selective functionalization of C(sp 2)–H
bonds assisted by the CONHR group is an appealing area. 9 For
instance, transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization of N-aryl phtha-
lazinones or pyridazinones with di ﬀerent coupling agents con-
tinues to attract wide interest. 10 In 2018, Ji and co-workers
reported a Rh( III)-catalyzed oxidant-free [4 + 1] annulation reac-
tion of N-aryl phthalazinones/pyridazinones and propargyl
alcohols for the formation of divergent heterocycles
(Scheme 1, eqn (1)). 11 Afterward, Sakhuja and co-workers
developed a tandem C –H/N–H activation reaction between
N-aryl phthalazinones and α-diazo carbonyl compounds to
aﬀord two di ﬀerent products by changing the types of addi-
tives (eqn (2)). 12 Moreover, they also described Ru( II)-catalyzed
carbocyclization of N-aryl phthalazinones with aryl isocyanates
(eqn (3)). 13 Based on the above discussion and our previous
research in the field of transition metal-catalyzed C –H bond
activation,14 herein, we disclosed an e ﬃcient Rh( III)-catalyzed
oxidative cyclization of N-aryl phthalazinones and pyridazi-
nones with various allenes to a ﬀord indazole derivatives.
Results and discussion
Initially, 2-phenyl-2,3-dihydrophthalazine-1,4-dione 1a and
buta-2,3-dien-1-ylbenzene 2a were chosen as the model sub-
strates to achieve the optimized reaction conditions (Table 1).
The substrates were treated with [Cp*RhCl 2]2 (2.5 mol%) and
AgOAc (1.0 equiv.) in MeCN (1.0 mL) at 100 °C for 12 h. The

Methoxyl substituted 1c was readily converted to the corres-
ponding regioisomers 3c and 3c′ in 70% (9 : 1) yield under the
optimized conditions. With regard to m-Me substituted 1d,
only one isomer 3d was a ﬀorded in 79% yield. When N-aryl
phthalazinones 1 possess electron-donating or electron-with-
drawing groups at the para position, such as alkyl ( –Me),
fluoro ( –F), chloro ( –Cl) and bromo ( –Br) groups, the reaction
oﬀered the corresponding products ( 3e–3h)i n4 7 –76% yields
under appropriate conditions. The disubstituted substrate 1i
was also well tolerated, forming the desired compound 3i in
62% yield. When electron-donating groups ( –Me) and electron-
withdrawing groups ( –Cl) were introduced to the phthalazine
moiety, smooth conversions were observed to obtain the
desired products 3j and 3k in 87% and 77% yields, respect-
ively. However, the products 3j and 3k were obtained as mix-
tures of two regioisomers in the same ratio; perhaps their start-
ing substrates 1j and 1k were prepared as an inseparable
regioisomeric mixture. We were pleased to observe that 3l and
3m were obtained in moderate yields. It is worth noting that
synthetic derivatives containing an N-aryl pyridazinone core
are an attractive area due to their broad range of pharma-
ceutical and agrochemical properties. 15 The substrates with
various electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups at
the aryl moiety undergo [4 + 1] cyclization, a ﬀording the
corresponding products 3n–3w in 52%–68% yields.
To further expand the versatility of this Rh(
III)-catalyzed [4 +
1] annulation reaction, we evaluated the scope of allenes
(Scheme 3). It was found that electron-donating ( –Me) or elec-
tron-deficient ( –F) substituents at the 2-position of allene gave
the desired products 4a and 4b in 90% and 75% yields,
respectively. Substrates 2 possessing methyl ( –Me), methoxy
(–OMe), chloro ( –Cl) and bromo ( –Br) at the meta-position
reacted favourably to provide the corresponding products 4c–4f
in 64–83% yields. When methyl ( –Me), fluoro ( –F), chloro ( –Cl)
and bromo ( –Br) were introduced at the para-position, the
desired products 4g–4j were obtained in 61% –80% yields.
Similarly, 1-naphthyl- or 2-naphthyl-group-substituted allenes
were well tolerated, a ﬀording the cyclization products 4k and
4l in 52% and 73% yields, respectively. When a long chain aryl
substituted substrate 2n was used, the target product 4m was
obtained with good selectivity (the E/Z ratio was determined by
1H NMR, E/Z = 9 : 1) in 83% yield. Pleasantly, aliphatic allene
was suitable for the catalytic system and formed the desired
compound 4n in 46% yield, indicating that conjugated olefin
as a substrate is not a required driver for the catalytic system.
However, the present reaction failed to a ﬀord the desired
annulation products with 1,1,4-trisubstituted and simple ali-
phatic allenes containing an ester group.
The synthetic e ﬀectiveness of the reaction was proved by
performing a gram-scale reaction between 1a and 2a to obtain
3a in 77% yield (Scheme 4a). Additionally, we also tried to
conduct a derivatization study of product 3a to further explore
the synthetic value of the reaction. Product 3a could react with
NaIO
4 in the presence of RuCl 3, obtaining the corresponding
product 5 (Scheme 4b).
In order to gain deeper insight into the reaction mecha-
nism, various control experiments were performed (Scheme 5).
First, a remarkable deuterium incorporation (55% D) in the
ortho-C–H bonds of 1e-d2 was observed in the presence of
CD3OD. The reaction of 1a with 2a in the presence of CD 3OD
for 12 h led to the formation of deuterio-3a with the deuterium
incorporation at the ortho-position of the N-aryl ring (10% D)
and the methyl group of product 3a (20% D). These results
indicated that the C –H bond cleavage step might be reversible
and the Rh –H intermediate was formed in the reaction
(Scheme 5a). In addition, the kinetic isotope e ﬀect values were
found to be 2.3 from competition experiments and two parallel
runs (Scheme 5b). These values suggest that the C –H bond
cleavage is probably involved in the turnover-limiting step.
Afterward, an equimolar amount of 1e and 1f was used,
aﬀording 3e and 3f with a ratio of 1.3 : 1 (Scheme 5c). The
result showed that an electron-donating group tended to favor
the reaction. Moreover, radical inhibition studies have shown
that the experiment does not involve radical processes
(Scheme 5d).

Based on our preliminary mechanistic studies and the pre-
vious literature, 8c,12,16 a plausible mechanism for Rh( III)-cata-
lyzed [4 + 1] annulation of N-aryl phthalazinones and pyridazi-
nones with allenes is described in Scheme 6. First, substrate
1a reacts with active rhodium, produced in situ through ion
exchange of [Cp*RhCl
2]2 with AgOAc and NaOAc, to form inter-
mediate I. Then, insertion of allene 2a followed by β-hydride
elimination o ﬀers intermediate III. The Rh –H in intermediate
III is inserted into the diene moiety to constitute IV, which
then undergoes reductive elimination to give compound 3a.
The Rh( I) species generated from the catalytic cycle is reoxi-
dized by AgOAc and NaOAc to give active rhodium.
Conclusions
In conclusion, we have successfully developed a Rh( III)-cata-
lyzed C –H oxidative cyclization of N-aryl phthalazinones and
pyridazinones with a variety of allenes. A variety of indazole
derivatives were constructively synthesized in moderate to
excellent yields. This catalytic system exhibits excellent func-
tional group tolerance and atom economy. Further evaluation
of the suitability of this catalytic system is currently being
carried out in our laboratory.
Experimental section
The general procedure for the C –H/N–H activation of N-aryl
phthalazinone 1a with allene 2a is as follows. A mixture of
2-phenyl-2,3-dihydrophthalazine-1,4-dione 1a (47.6 mg,
0.20 mmol), buta-2,3-dien-1-ylbenzene 2a (39.1 mg,
0.30 mmol), [Rh*CpCl 2]2 (3.1 mg, 2.5 mol%), NaOAc (16.4 mg,
0.20 mmol) and AgOAc (33.4 mg, 0.20 mmol) in MeCN
(1.0 mL) was stirred at 120 °C under open air for 12 hours. The
resulting mixture was cooled to room temperature, the solvent
was removed under vacuum and the crude reaction mixture
was purified by silica gel (200 –300 mesh) column chromato-
graphy using hexane/ethyl acetate (6 : 1) as the eluant to a ﬀord
3a as a yellow solid.
Author contributions
Chuanming Yu conceived this work. Chuanliu Yin,
Tianshuo Zhong and Xiangyun Zheng performed the experi-
ments. Lihao Li and Jian Zhou analyzed the data and prepared
the ESI. Chuanliu Yin and Xiangyun Zheng wrote this manu-
script. All authors read and approved the final version to be
published.
